inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,809,663,075 issued less 16,649,328 treasury = 1,793.0m outstanding at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2026 tanshin), plus 6.0m dilutive potential shares (FY2025 diluted-EPS table). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks are negligible (JPY 0.7bn FY2025) so the flat count is a modelling convention, not a funded one.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual tanshin, statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payments' JPY 3,069m (4503.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:874); no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). Astellas is a near-SBC-zero filer: 0.14% of revenue.
inputs.fy0_note: Repo label FY2025 = fiscal year ended 31 March 2026. Guidance year FY2026 = year ending 31 March 2027.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.7% risk-free, 5.5% ERP, beta ~0.75 for a large-cap pharma gives a textbook CoE near 6% and a WACC near 5.5%; house uses 7.0% across all three scenarios, a deliberate ~1.5pp premium for a single-product (XTANDI ~45% of revenue) franchise entering loss of exclusivity, but well below the 9% JPY keiretsu-industrial reference because prescription oncology demand is non-cyclical. The same WACC is used in bear and bull: cliff timing and depth are charged in the flows, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. IFRS 16 filer. FY2025 lease principal JPY 15,476m (financing CF) + interest on lease liabilities JPY 4,028m (audited note 15) = JPY 19,504m = 0.91% of revenue, charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt (total_debt is bonds and borrowings only: JPY 589.9bn at 30 Jun 2026). D&A for cash tax is ex right-of-use depreciation: 194,594 - 15,874 ROU = 178,720 = 8.35% of FY2025 revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; the JPY 1.8bn non-controlling interest (30 Jun 2026) is deducted once in the equity bridge. Immaterial (~JPY 1/share).
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest and dividends received (JPY 6,063m FY2025) are classified in INVESTING cash flow under Astellas's IFRS presentation, so they are not inside reported OCF/FCF and nothing needs stripping; interest_income = 0 is a classification fact, not a materiality judgment. The company is net debt (JPY 345bn), so the net-cash double-count rule does not arise either.
inputs.ebitda_basis: EBITDA margin path is IFRS-16, pre-impairment: FY2025 operating profit 382,633 + D&A 194,594 + impairment losses 54,187 = 631,414 = 29.5% of revenue. Core operating profit (555.7bn) + core-basis D&A (~75bn) reconciles to the same figure. FY2026 guidance (core OP 620bn, full OP 395bn after ~140bn acquired-intangible amortisation and ~80bn provision for impairment/restructuring) implies ~29-30%; Y1 is set at 29.0% to haircut the cash portion of the 80bn restructuring provision.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax rate 24% in Y1 rising to 25%: FY2025 income tax paid JPY 98,612m on an engine-basis EBIT of ~JPY 430bn = 23%; FY2026 guidance implies (385 PBT - 300 profit)/385 = 22% book rate. Global mix (US 44%, Japan 14% at 30.6% statutory, Europe ~25%). No NOL or valuation-allowance distortion.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md: JPY-built WACC, single lease treatment (B), NCI once in the bridge, FVTOCI cross-shareholdings added to the bridge because their dividend income sits outside operating flows, SBC rows kept explicit at 0.14%). First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). The build is a product-level revenue model collapsed into the growth path: XTANDI (JPY 960.8bn FY2025, 45% of revenue) loses US price protection from January 2027 (Medicare IRA negotiated price; management's guided -5.3% for FY2026) and US generic enzalutamide entry is assumed in FY2027 (year to March 2028), with ex-US erosion following; Strategic Brands (PADCEV, IZERVAY, VYLOY, VEOZAH, XOSPATA; JPY 480.3bn FY2025, guided +27% to 610.0bn FY2026) grow 20%/15%/12%/10%/8%/6% thereafter, reaching the >50%-of-revenue-by-2030 management target in the base case; legacy brands (Prograf, mirabegron, Vesicare, others; ~JPY 700bn) decline 2-3%/yr. Pipeline (ASP2138 and other Phase 3 starts) and the large acquisition management says it is open to are NOT modelled: the cash they would consume and the revenue they would add are both outside the explicit flows. Buybacks negligible; buyback_cash JPY 730m FY2025 recorded for the reader.
inputs.price_note: Price from the Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; a regular-session TSE close, not an after-hours print. 52-week range 1,595.5 - 2,717.0.

equity_bridge.item: Equity instruments at FVTOCI (cross-shareholdings, quoted 8,382 + unquoted 30,135)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 audited report note on financial instruments, fair value at 31 March 2026; their dividend income is in investing cash flow, outside the modelled operating flows (matching-asset rule)
30 June 2026 balance sheet; charged once here, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-scenario explicit product build (XTANDI loss of exclusivity netted against Strategic Brand growth), 10-year revenue CAGR; historical CAGRs are not a forward proxy for a company about to lose patent protection on 45% of revenue
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.7% is less than half the revenue 5yr CAGR 11.4%: FY2020-FY2025 revenue growth was XTANDI/PADCEV ramp plus yen weakness (FY2025 alone +JPY 30.1bn from FX), while equity growth was held back by the FY2023-FY2024 impairment cycle (Xyphos, AT132, Agensys; JPY 187.6bn impairment in FY2024 alone) and a ~48% dividend payout. EPS 3yr CAGR of 44% is off the depressed FY2022 base (JPY 54.09) and is not a trend.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income is outside OCF by presentation). SBC is 0.1-0.2% of revenue throughout, so the owner and reported series are within 0.2pp of each other. FY2025 owner FCF of JPY 472bn (22% of revenue) includes ~JPY 27bn of working-capital inflow (refund liabilities +43bn, receivables -64bn, inventories -16bn) and a further +64bn of 'other' operating items; the component build's year-one FCF (~JPY 415bn, 18.7%) deliberately does not carry those forward.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2026 guidance (revenue JPY 2,220bn, +3.8%: XTANDI 910 / Strategic Brands 610 / other ~700). Y2-Y5 product build (JPY bn): XTANDI 637 / 382 / 287 / 244 (-30%, -40%, -25%, -15%: US IRA price from Jan-2027, US generic entry FY2027, ex-US erosion FY2028+); Strategic Brands 732 / 842 / 943 / 1,037 (+20/15/12/10%); legacy 679 / 659 / 639 / 626 (-3%, -3%, -3%, -2%). Totals 2,048 / 1,883 / 1,869 / 1,907. Strategic Brands reach 54% of revenue in FY2030, in line with the >50%-by-2030 target. Y6-Y10 +2-2.7% as Strategic Brand growth (8%, 6%) fades toward their own 2030s exclusivity expiries and XTANDI settles at a generic-era tail.
base.margin_rationale: 29.0% Y1 vs FY2025 29.5% (pre-impairment) and FY2026 guidance ~29-30% (core OP 620bn, SG&A -7% from SMT, R&D +12.8%). Trough 24.0% in Y4: US XTANDI profit is shared 50/50 with Pfizer so the contribution lost is roughly half the revenue lost, while R&D (~JPY 330-355bn) is sticky. Recovery to 26.0% by Y8 as Strategic Brands scale and SMT savings persist; never back to the FY2025-26 peak because PADCEV is also a Pfizer profit-share and Japan NHI revisions compound.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A ex-ROU 8.35% FY2025, rising to 9.5% in Y3 as the ~JPY 140bn acquired-intangible amortisation (IZERVAY/Iveric, others) is spread over a smaller revenue base, then declining to 6.0% as those intangibles roll off. Capex 4.0% (FY2025: PPE 57.7bn + intangibles 26.9bn = 84.6bn, 4.0%; FY2024 3.0%). The terminal D&A-capex gap (2pp) is sunk acquisition amortisation, not an under-investment assumption.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables + inventories JPY 1,078bn against payables JPY 200bn at March 2026: growth consumes cash, so wc_capture is -15% of the revenue change; in the FY2027-28 contraction years working capital releases cash, which is what a receivables unwind on falling XTANDI sales does.

bull.growth_rationale: US generic enzalutamide entry slips to FY2028 (formulation-patent litigation holds), XTANDI erodes -15%/-25%/-20% rather than -30/-40/-25; Strategic Brands beat (PADCEV MIBC expansion with Keytruda, VYLOY CLDN18.2 testing penetration, IZERVAY) at +25/20/15/12%; ASP2138 and other Phase 3 starts begin contributing from FY2030. Revenue troughs at ~JPY 2,170bn in Y3 and is back above FY2025 by Y5.
bull.margin_rationale: Margins hold 27-28%: SMT savings compound, Strategic Brand mix improves, yen stays at or above 150/USD.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 misses on an H2 XTANDI step-down larger than guided; US generics arrive on schedule and erosion is -45%/-45%/-30% (XTANDI JPY ~500bn -> ~190bn by FY2029); Strategic Brands slow to +15/10/8/6% (Keytruda-combination share in bladder cancer, VEOZAH hepatic label, IZERVAY competition from Syfovre); legacy brands -5%/yr on Japan NHI G1 cuts; yen strengthens toward 135/USD. Revenue troughs near JPY 1,660bn and barely grows thereafter.
bear.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin falls to 20.5% with R&D held at ~JPY 350bn on a shrinking base and no further SMT offsets; cap 13x and terminal growth 1.0% because the terminal business is a sub-scale pharma with a thin late-stage pipeline.

scenario_narratives.base: The question is whether JPY 480bn of Strategic Brands can replace a JPY 960bn XTANDI franchise that loses US price protection in January 2027 (IRA) and US exclusivity about a year later. Base says they largely do by scale but not by profit: revenue troughs ~12% below FY2025 in FY2028 and recovers only slowly, the EBITDA margin troughs at 24% because half of US XTANDI's profit was Pfizer's anyway while R&D is sticky, and Strategic Brands pass 50% of revenue in FY2030 as management targets. No pipeline or acquisition value is included; the terminal value is capped at 15x year-10 FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Formulation-patent litigation keeps US generic enzalutamide out until FY2028 and PADCEV's muscle-invasive bladder cancer expansion plus VYLOY's CLDN18.2 penetration push Strategic Brands to +25%/+20%; SMT keeps the margin near 28%; ASP2138 and other Phase 3 starts begin contributing from 2030. Revenue is back above FY2025 by FY2030.
scenario_narratives.bear: XTANDI erodes faster and earlier than guided on both sides of the Pacific, Keytruda combinations take bladder-cancer share from PADCEV, VEOZAH and IZERVAY disappoint on label and competition, Japan NHI revisions keep cutting the legacy book, and the yen strengthens. Revenue falls ~22% from FY2025 to a sub-JPY 1.7tn base with a 20-21% margin, and the company's own openness to a large acquisition becomes a value-destroying 'rescue BD' rather than a growth lever.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: a known-date loss of exclusivity on ~45% of revenue, the uncertain US generic timing, an R&D record of repeated impairments (Xyphos, AT132, Agensys, Seattle site closure) and a CEO who has publicly left a large acquisition on the table together make the downside path more than a tail. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: a patent-litigation win on XTANDI, Strategic Brands beating a 27% guide, and the pipeline converting. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Astellas is priced as a patent-cliff story and the house base case agrees with that price almost exactly: the market is paying roughly the probability-weighted value of the explicit XTANDI run-off plus Strategic Brand replacement, with no credit for pipeline or acquisition upside and no penalty for acquisition risk. The valuation is therefore a bet on cliff timing and depth and on Strategic Brand execution, not on a re-rating. House and street bases coincide to within JPY ~25/share because SBC is 0.14% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: XTANDI US generic entry timing (FY2027 assumed; litigation could move it a year either way, worth roughly JPY 150-250/share per year of exclusivity)
Strategic Brand growth below the +27% FY2026 guide (PADCEV vs Keytruda combinations, VEOZAH hepatic label, IZERVAY competition)
A large acquisition to fill the XTANDI gap, which management has not ruled out, funded from the balance sheet the bridge credits
FX: a JPY reporter with ~85% non-Japan revenue; FY2026 guidance assumes 150/USD and 180/EUR; a 10% yen appreciation is a ~5-6% hit to EBITDA
Japan NHI price revisions (FY2026 ~4% average cut, G1 rule now on biologics) and US IRA negotiation extending to Strategic Brands

R&D productivity: FY2023-FY2024 impairments totalled over JPY 240bn; the model assumes 4% of revenue in capex/intangibles sustains the pipeline, which history says is optimistic without further write-downs
